title: Journey into Product Management
text: Medium Journey into Product Management. The thought of pursuing it clung… | by Fiyinfoluwa Olaleye | Sep, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Fiyinfoluwa Olaleye Fiyinfoluwa Olaleye Product Management Fiyinfoluwa Olaleye 2 min read · Just now -- Listen Share For a long time, tech seemed like something that would never be for me. Maybe I liked it for others, but I battled with the idea of learning or practising it. Then, a few people suggested Product Management, and I finally checked what it was about. Guess what I discovered? It is not bad after all. I already had some transferable skills. However, different circumstances stopped me from learning after applying in 2024 and 2025. The thought of pursuing it clung tightly to me, so I gave it another shot this year, and I got in. So, after several years of trying to learn Product Management, I eventually began the journey in March 2026. Press enter or click to view image in full size Image from Google The journey has been a mix of everything, sincerely. But as I continue to learn, my findings have further opened my eyes to the necessity of learning product management. As someone who has worked with cross-functional teams, planned and led projects, led teams, and managed stakeholder relationships, product management feels so right! So, I'll be taking you through my product management journey. I'll try to start from the beginning and continue from there. Why am I just starting this since I started classes in April? Well, don't judge me. Life was tight when I started, and I couldn't even think of doing this. Let's just say I'm more settled to accommodate the demands of doing this. Why am I doing this? As someone who enjoys storytelling, I want to document the journey publicly. Besides, why not? The idea of sharing the journey felt right, so I obliged. There’s no harm in sharing, after all. Also, I would be sharing applicable life lessons beyond the technical parts of my PM journey. Lack of knowledge sometimes breeds hesitance. Maybe brooding over and researching that idea more is the clarity you need.
